d1m1-role.lead: Case Management is the **end-to-end coordination** of a case from intake to resolution: tracking, handling and moving it, phase by phase.

concepts.text: Timely progression, proper documentation and compliance, clear communication: **the three tests** every task on the file must pass
Six stages, from Intake & Case Opening to Billing, Resolution & Closing: **you carry the file** through all six
You build the plan and recommend next steps; **strategy itself stays** with Atty. Thorne
Reading the whole file for risk, not single tasks: **spotting the weak point** before it costs the client

framework.title: The General Process

steps.label: Intake & Case Opening
steps.text: Verify the facts, run the Conflict Check and open the file in the CMS

steps.label: Case Planning & Strategy Support
steps.text: Draft the Case Plan and recommend next steps; **Atty. Thorne sets strategy**

steps.label: Documentation & File Management
steps.text: Request, name and file every document; the CMS is the single source of truth

steps.label: Communication Management
steps.text: Keep the client, carriers and providers updated; log every contact the same day

steps.label: Case Monitoring & Tracking
steps.text: Docket every deadline, watch progress and flag risk to counsel the day you see it

steps.label: Billing, Resolution & Closing
steps.text: Support the billing and lien records through resolution, then close a complete file

framework.note: Six stages on one track, from opening the file to closing it.

d1m1-case.lead: Every file is worked from **its verified facts**: who was hurt, how, which policies apply, and what could weaken the claim.

concepts.text: Parties, date of loss, SOL, client position and coverage on one card: **the facts every task reads**
How, where and when the collision happened, confirmed by the Police Report and witnesses; **ambiguity here needs counsel**
The one fact the defense will build on; name it early so **counsel plans around it**
Intake sheet, supplement and Police Report are the file's sources: **quote the document**, never your memory

framework.title: The Structured Intake Questions
head: Question
On this file
rows: Who
John Doe, client; Robert Smith, defendant; **the Police Report** names the rest
What
A two-vehicle collision; what EMS found is in the Run Report
When
Where
The all-way stop at Maple Hollow Rd & Birch Ave
How
How it happened, and any citation: **read the Police Report**
framework.note: Every answer comes from a document; ambiguous facts of loss or liability go to Atty. Thorne for review.

d1m1-l1.lead: Intake is where you establish **control, structure and clarity**: verifying facts and mapping every party to the policy it unlocks.

concepts.text: Every policy that can pay the claim, layered in the order it pays; **find every layer** at intake
The at-fault driver's coverage for injuries he causes others: **the first layer** to pay, and a third-party claim
First-party cover for when the at-fault driver's BI is **missing or too small**; reached through the vehicle or household
A signed UM rejection or an owned-vehicle exclusion **closes a layer**; record the document that does it
First-party medical coverage paid regardless of fault: **it pays bills first**, while the claim is still open
PD liability repairs what the at-fault driver damaged; collision is the owner's own cover. **Neither joins the injury stack**
A split limit caps each injured person at the first figure and **the whole accident** at the second; read both
The carrier's statement of the named insured, covered vehicles, coverages and limits: **written proof of coverage**

framework.title: The Intake Workflow

steps.label: Raw File Received
steps.text: The file arrives from “On the Records”; read it end to end first

steps.label: Review & Verify Details
steps.text: Check the DOL, parties and signatures against the Police Report, not the intake note

steps.label: Conflict Check Completed
steps.text: Run it on every party's **full legal name**; log its date and result

steps.label: Approved or Escalated
steps.text: Complete intake moves to acceptance; incomplete intake goes back, uncertain eligibility to Atty. Thorne

steps.label: File Created and Logged
steps.text: Open the matter in the CMS: six roles mapped, SOL docketed, documents named

framework.note: Nothing moves before the Conflict Check is documented; coverage is then read off the Declaration Page.

d1m1-l2.lead: Before clinical planning, the **Regulatory Triple-Check** establishes the claim and your authority to act; the Payer Order then decides who funds care.

concepts.text: A payer's right to stand in the client's shoes and **recover what it paid** for accident care
Deciding which payer is billed first, so each bill **goes to the right payer** and nothing is paid twice
The firm's written promise to pay a provider from the settlement: **last in the Payer Order**
What the client keeps once fees, costs and liens are paid: **a late-flagged lien** comes straight out of it

framework.title: The Regulatory Triple-Check
head: Check
What you do
Why it matters
rows: HIPAA Compliance
Obtain a claim-specific authorization naming the incident date
A standard release may not be adequate for injury claims
Medicare/Medicaid Reporting
If 65+ or on SSDI, report the case to the BCRC
Avoids federal penalties and **settlement freezes** under MMSEA
Subrogation Management
Set the Payer Order: PIP/MedPay → private health insurance → LOP/provider liens
Each bill reaches the right payer; reimbursement rights surface early
framework.note: Clear all three before clinical planning begins: the claim is established and you are authorized to act.

d1m2-l1.lead: The No Contact Protocol is a **formal due-diligence record**: it tracks silence, proves the firm tried, and protects it from liability.

concepts.text: Points where work slows, stalls or turns inconsistent; **a silent client** is one, delaying case progression
Proof the firm made reasonable, documented efforts to reach the client: **the record that justifies** whatever comes next
The contact methods the client and firm agreed at intake; **only approved channels** count as a valid attempt
A second person, collected at intake, who can **still reach the client** after they go quiet

framework.title: Common Intake Bottlenecks
head: Bottleneck
How it shows up
rows: Incomplete Client Information
Missing contact details or incident facts; no supporting documents
Delayed Client Follow-Up
**Unanswered clarification requests**, missed verification calls, slow documents
Conflict Check Delays
System backlog, incomplete entries, unclear opposing party information
Intake Form Errors
Incorrect dates, inconsistent statements, missing signatures, misfiled records
Case Eligibility Uncertainty
Ambiguous facts of loss or liability needing attorney review
Communication Gaps
Incomplete intake packets; miscommunication between departments
framework.note: A silent client is Delayed Client Follow-Up: the No Contact Protocol clears it, one logged attempt at a time.

d1m2-l2.lead: The Final Warning Letter **closes the outreach record**: one last documented notice before the firm searches for the client or counsel moves to withdraw.

concepts.text: Certified mail proves delivery; email gets a response. **Each covers the other's gap**
An AND gate, not a checklist: the search waits until **all three are true**, so money isn't spent early
A paid search for a missing person's current address and contacts; **counsel authorizes it** because it spends firm money
Ending representation by Notice of Withdrawal or Motion to Withdraw; **only the attorney decides**, under firm and court rules

framework.title: The No Contact Protocol, Steps 4–6

steps.label: Final Warning Letter
steps.text: Earlier attempts itemized, a 7–14 day deadline, withdrawal notice; certified mail AND email

steps.label: Decision Point
steps.text: Still no response: **the attorney decides** on a Notice or Motion to Withdraw

steps.label: File Closure
steps.text: Marked “No response – withdrew per protocol”; proof of every attempt retained

framework.note: Skip-tracing waits for all three: ladder exhausted, letter sent, deadline passed. Counsel authorizes it.

d1m3-l1.lead: Client instructions protect the claim from **the client's own good intentions**: what the client says, posts, signs or skips can become evidence.

concepts.text: A medical danger threatens the client's health; a legal danger, like **a gap in care**, threatens the claim
Everything on the file can reach defense counsel, so instructions stay **factual, never legal opinion**
The notice that the firm represents the client; from then on, adverse contact **routes through the firm**
The authorized daily rate and number of days; **anything beyond them** is the client's own cost

framework.title: The Rental Authorization Check

steps.label: Whose Policy Is Primary?
steps.text: The renter's own policy is usually primary; the rental company follows a written denial

steps.label: Who Authorizes?
steps.text: Confirm who authorizes the rental and check for a rental reimbursement endorsement

steps.label: Daily Rate Cap
steps.text: Record the authorized daily rate before the client collects a vehicle

steps.label: Duration Limit
steps.text: Record the number of covered days: **uncovered days are the client's cost**

framework.note: All four go in the CMS before collection; the LOR carve-out lets the carrier discuss only Property Damage.

d1m3-l2.lead: Property Damage is **a separate claim** with its own measure: repair or total, set against the vehicle's pre-loss value.

concepts.text: Photos, video and damage must match how the crash happened; **the physics must be possible**
The initial estimate prices visible damage; a supplemental after teardown is **proof of impact severity**
Past the repair-to-ACV threshold the carrier pays ACV from its Valuation Report: **verify it line by line**
A comparable vehicle while the client's is out: confirm who authorizes it, **the daily cap and duration**

framework.title: Property Damage (PD) Deep Dive
head: Check
What you audit
Why it matters
rows: Photos
Point-of-impact clarity, including the undercarriage and frame
Physical proof of the impact behind the injury claim
Estimates vs. Actuals
The insurance estimate against the final body shop bill
**Supplementals prove hidden** structural damage
Total Loss/Value
The CCC One or other Valuation Report, line by line
So the client isn't lowballed on the vehicle's value
The Scene Audit
Photos, video and damage against how the crash happened
The physics of the claim must be possible
framework.note: Audit Property Damage as carefully as the medicals: it is physical evidence of how hard the impact was.

d1m4-l1.lead: Early evaluation joins **coverage, liability and projection**: is there money, who is responsible, and how the case is likely to move.

concepts.text: Which policies apply, with what benefits, limits and exclusions: **is there money** to pay the claim?
Who caused the incident and to what degree: **clear, shared or disputed**, and on what evidence
An early read of risk and trajectory from coverage, liability, injury, treatment and documents; **value stays with counsel**
In a legal framework, Case Management shifts from **best efforts to strict compliance**: every plan deadline is docketed

framework.title: Why These Three Work Together
head: Element
The question
What you check
rows: Coverage
Is there money to pay the claim?
Valid policies, coverage type, limits, exclusions and gaps
Liability
Who is responsible, and to what degree?
Who caused it; clear, shared or disputed; evidence; comparative negligence
Projection
How is this case likely to move?
Coverage, liability, injury severity, treatment expectations, documentation quality
framework.note: Projection reads risk and trajectory; it stays preliminary until coverage is confirmed, and case value stays with Atty. Thorne.

d1m4-l2.lead: A Case Plan is a **living, approved document**: drafted in structure, reviewed by counsel, then run.

concepts.text: One structure for every plan, so reviewers can **scan it fast** and nothing is missed
Draft, route, review, approve, execute; **a return is normal**, a step back into drafting, not a failure
A conclusion still awaiting its proof; when the proof arrives and differs, **the plan is re-routed**
The CMS keeps every version unaltered, so **each approval is provable**, and every note is discoverable

framework.title: Mandatory Disclosure & Compliance Tracking
head: Requirement
What the plan tracks
rows: Electronic Record Integrity
A CMS that keeps an **unalterable audit trail** of every version
State-Specific Timelines
Carrier-mandated deadlines, such as an early IME in no-fault states
Letter of Protection (LOP)
Providers treating under an LOP, so no bill arrives as a surprise
The Golden Rule
Medical plan and legal claim as parallel tracks: coordinate, don't commingle
framework.note: The file is discoverable in litigation: write every plan note as if defense counsel will read it.

d1m1-upl.lead: UPL is giving legal advice without a license; a Case Manager stays on **the fact side** of that line, every time.

concepts.text: Telling the client what a record says: a date, an amount, **what was sent**, and when
What happens next, what a form is for, and **who decides**; never how it ends
Any opinion on what his facts mean for **his rights, money or choices**: the attorney's alone
An opinion question is written down word for word and **sent to Atty. Thorne** the same day
